CFD_Automation · Stage 2 · refine map · from the Stage 1 section tables · 3 Nov 2026 · updated 9 Nov 2026

Where to refine: transition, bubbles and separation, per wing

The transition band of the mesh is generic: one band for every wing. First (2–3 Nov) it was upper surface 0–85 % c, lower 60–100 % c. Since 7 Nov the lower band runs from the leading edge, 0–100 % c (decision 74). The upper band was written 0–85 % c until 8 Nov, but as built the upper side got band-size cells to the trailing edge too, because both sides share one node list; since 8 Nov it is written 0–100 % c (owner), and since 9 Nov the band is on for every run, SA and LM alike (decision 81). So this map no longer sets the band; it shows where transition and bubbles sit inside it. This page reads the Stage 1 section tables for one wing at a time and shows where the flow turns turbulent, where the laminar bubbles sit and where it separates, strip by strip. First section: the map at the four Re levels on the mean chord (7 Nov, new). Below it, the interactive first-approach map, kept as the record.

Refine map at the Re levels (7 Nov; redone 8 Nov at the new levels)

What was done. The map has a Re mode now (similarity, decision 70): each of the 20 reference wings (5 per type, the new picks) at the four Re levels on the mean chord (10⁵, 3 × 10⁵, 10⁶, 4 × 10⁶ since 8 Nov; the 7 Nov run at 1.5 × 10⁶ and 3 × 10⁶ is kept in data/studies/refine_map_re_levels_7nov.json) and root angles −5° to 12°, at unit mean chord and sea level, with the 2-D section tables read at Mach 0.1 and rebuilt on the fixed nose (decision 64). 13 strips per half wing (3 per panel). For each wing, Re level, strip and side: where transition sits from −5° to 8° (and to 12°); the band it needs, as before (transition ± 10 % c, the bubbles, the separation start); whether the bands hold it; and the strips with no XFOIL answer. Then an as-built check on 16 built surfaces (wing 0 of each type at the four Re levels, level VC). In the figures, the upper band is the one written until 8 Nov, 0–85 % c (since 8 Nov written 0–100 % c, owner: every band now fits). Code: the Re mode of cfdauto/mesh/refine_map.py; scripts/refine_map_re.py; data data/studies/refine_map_re.json; note decisions/refine_map_re.md.

What it showsMedian transition position over the 65 strips of each type (5 wings × 13 strips) against the root angle, at the four Re levels on the mean chord, upper and lower side, with the decided bands: upper 0–85 % c (shaded: beyond it), lower 0–100 % c.

ConclusionThe upper transition moves aft as the angle and the Re fall: at 10⁵ its median sits at 88–100 % c at −5° on every type, past the upper band's end; the lower transition comes to the leading edge at negative angles (median 0–29 % c at −5°), which the lower band 0–100 % c holds.

ConclusionAs written, the upper band misses the upper transition on most strips at 10⁵ and 3 × 10⁵ (0–49 % fit, short by up to 15 % c, to the trailing edge) and on 0–88 % at 10⁶ and 4 × 10⁶; as built this is no gap, because the shared node distribution (decision 60) and the lower band 0–100 % c already give the upper side band cells to the trailing edge.

What it showsShare of strips with no XFOIL answer against the root angle, per type and Re level; no strip is below the tables' lowest Re, so each one is beyond the section's 2-D stall or a failed point.

ConclusionOnly the tailless wings lose answers in numbers, at negative root angles (up to 46 % of the BWB and 42 % of the flying-wing strips at −5°), where their outboard sections (MH 61, MH 60 / MH 45) are below the lowest angle XFOIL converges at; the band there rests on the other angles.

As built (7 Nov)On all 16 built surfaces at VC (all passed every check) the largest upper cell over 85–99.5 % c is 0.950–0.995 × the band cell: the upper side already has band-size cells to the trailing edge, because both sides of a ring share one node list (decision 60) and the lower band is 0–100 % c. So no mesh change is needed. Written as 0–100 % c, the 16 surfaces come out the same (the same ring counts, no node moved by more than 1.4 × 10⁻¹³ c, round-off). That holds at VC only. On the 20 reference wings × 4 Re (7 Nov): at VC the same mesh to round-off (80 of 80 with the same counts, no node moved by more than 3.0 × 10⁻¹³ c); at F, 0–100 % c adds 2 ring nodes on 42 of 80 builds (0.39 % more cells, median; 0.55 % at most), because with 0–85 % c the upper cells over 85–100 % c at F can sit a little above the band cell, inside the 1 % check (on BWB reference wing 0 at Re 3 × 10⁵: 0.00501 c against 0.0050 c). On 8 Nov the owner wrote the upper band as 0–100 % c, and the screen was re-run (Stage 2 Study 12): 2 more ring nodes on VC 44 of 782, C 3 of 80, M 24 of 80, F 383 of 782 meshes (every set at VC and F, the reference wings at C and M), cells at most +1.1 %. Data: data/studies/upper_band_check.json.

Limits. 2-D strips (XFOIL e^N, N_crit 9: calm air) with one uniform induced angle; no crossflow transition on swept panels, no 3-D relief of bubbles, no tip effects: where to look, not the 3-D answer. A strip without an answer at one angle drops out at that angle only. The as-built check covers wing 0 of each type. The per-wing band stays a candidate (decision 65) until a 3-D transition check.

What the envelope costs and saves

Every strip, at this condition and over the envelope

Limits of this map

  • 2-D strips: each strip is an XFOIL run of its section, free transition with N_crit 9 (calm air). Gusty air (N_crit 5) moves transition forward and shortens the laminar run; add margin for it.
  • One induced angle for the whole wing (elliptic): the local angle of attack along the semi-span is root angle + twist − that one number. On swept and tapered wings the real local angle differs along the semi-span; the tip is usually unloaded more than this says.
  • No crossflow transition on swept panels, no 3-D relief of bubbles, no tip vortex. Panels swept over about 25° with Re normal to the edge above 10⁶ can transition near the leading edge; the generic band's 0 % c start on the upper surface covers that, this map does not.
  • Hatched strips had no XFOIL answer: past the section's 2-D stall, at high angle or at negative angle. At −5° these are mostly the washed-out outboard strips of the BWBs and flying wings (local angles −6° to −11°; some are below the tables' −10°). A strip with no answer anywhere in the range falls back to the generic band; a strip with some answers keeps only those.
  • The dataset is the Stage 1 section tables (14 Re × 3 Mach × 49 angles per section, trilinear lookup); a strip between two sections takes the blend of its parents' answers.

What would make it better, and stay cheap

  • AVL (vortex lattice) for the local angle. Replaces the one induced angle by a spanwise lift distribution that knows sweep, taper and twist: seconds per wing. Biggest correction on swept BWBs and on washed-out tips. Weak on the thick centre body (VLM sees only the camber line) and inviscid, so the strip lift must be fed back (a quasi-3D loop: section cl from the tables, AVL for the downwash, repeat).
  • NeuralFoil for the 2-D answer. A neural surrogate of XFOIL: milliseconds per strip, never fails to converge, takes the exact blended section instead of the parents' blend, and returns the boundary-layer state along the chord, from which separation and bubbles can be read. It inherits XFOIL's physics (2-D, e^N) and adds its own fit error, so check it against the tables on a sample first.
  • Neither fixes 3-D transition. Crossflow on swept panels and tip effects need a criterion of their own or a 3-D transition RANS check (γ-Re_θ in SU2) on a few wings before the per-wing band replaces the generic one. Until then the per-wing band is a candidate, not a rule.
Data: Stage_2_surface_mesh/data/studies/refine_map_reference.json from cfdauto.mesh.refine_map (the Stage 1 section tables through cfdauto.flowmap.engine), the 20 reference wings, Mach 0.03–0.20, −5…12° at the root, sea level, 3 strips per panel. Band cell = bubble length (Stage 1 table at the local Re) / 20, at the Mach of the slider. Page: scripts/make_refine_page.py.
